observation.visible_scene: A calm, slow-moving river or stream flanked by dense, bright-green summer trees on both banks under a pale sky. The water fills the lower half of the frame and mirrors the foliage and sky. A small rock protrudes from the left bank near mid-frame, a fallen log lies along the right bank, and a diagonal lens-flare streak with green and orange circular artifacts overlays the upper-left and left portions of the image. The composition is essentially a fixed landscape shot.
visible_changes: The overall framing, tree positions, bank objects, and lens-flare artifacts remain constant from the first to the last sampled frame, indicating no detectable camera pan, tilt, or zoom.
The water surface shows only very subtle, continuous shimmer/ripple distortion in the tree and sky reflections; the reflected shapes waver slightly but do not translate or deform dramatically.
A few tiny pale flecks (likely floating debris/leaves) on the water near the lower-center stay in roughly the same positions, with at most negligible drift.
No object enters or exits the frame, and no larger motion (swimming, falling, wind-blown branch movement) is discernible within the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the water's slight ripple pattern intensifies or calms outside this short window.
Whether the floating flecks actually drift downstream or are stationary reflections/compression noise.
Any audio, weather change, or movement beyond the cropped time boundaries.
uncertain_details: The apparent micro-changes in the reflections may be partly compression/rendering noise rather than physical water motion.
The exact motion state of the small surface flecks cannot be confirmed across frames.
Lens-flare artifacts appear static but their subtle brightness variation cannot be reliably measured.

do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.

properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from

background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
